args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
plan-deviation-report.docx

Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Work Product: Comparison of Committee Redlined Plan against Debtor Original Plan
Sources Relied Upon: Deal materials (base plan / disclosure-statement framework); Counterparty (committee) markup; Schedules and Exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B); Deal-team correspondence (controlling partner instruction). Misfiled unrelated correspondence in the matter folder was identified and disregarded.

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report reconciles the official committee of unsecured creditors' redlined Plan of Reorganization (the "Committee Markup") against the debtor's original Plan of Reorganization and related base materials (the "Debtor Plan"), as qualified by the disclosure schedules and exhibits and as prioritized by the controlling deal-team instruction.

The Committee Markup accepts most firm-standard / Debtor Plan architecture but introduces three material deviations that must be addressed before confirmation strategy and creditor negotiations proceed:

1. Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping basket.
2. Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this case, intersecting Schedule 3.7 disclosures.
3. Survival / limitation period — a shortened limitation period for core representations that contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner message): the client will concede the basket conversion, but any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not followed in this report.

Under the schedules: scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. Accordingly, Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B govern reconciliation of the MAE, indemnification, and survival deviations, respectively.

II. SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY

A. Documents Compared
- Debtor original Plan of Reorganization and related plan-support architecture reflected in the base deal materials (including the valuation summary, transmittal framing, and disclosure-statement excerpts referenced in the engagement instruction).
- Committee redlined Plan (counterparty markup).
- Disclosure schedules and exhibits qualifying the base materials: Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries); Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities); Exhibit B (survival matrix).
- Deal-team correspondence establishing current analysis priorities.

B. Method
For each deviation, this report: (i) states the Debtor Plan baseline; (ii) states the Committee Markup change; (iii) reconciles the change against the applicable schedule/exhibit; (iv) assesses commercial and confirmation risk; and (v) records a recommended disposition consistent with the controlling client instruction (Accept / Reject / Counter), with walk-away designation where instructed.

C. Materials Expressly Not Relied Upon
Administrative / misfiled correspondence from an unrelated engagement present in the matter folder was not used.

III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS

DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
Status: MATERIAL — Split disposition (cap: counter/reject reduction; basket: accept conversion per controlling instruction)

A. Debtor Plan Baseline
The Debtor Plan and firm-standard indemnity architecture provide:
- An indemnification cap at the negotiated baseline level supporting post-effective-date residual risk allocation among the reorganized debtor, plan sponsor / purchaser constituencies, and released parties as framed in the disclosure materials.
- A deductible (true deductible) basket: indemnifiable losses accrue only above the basket threshold; amounts within the basket are not recoverable and do not "tip" recovery of the entire loss stack from dollar one.

B. Committee Markup
- Silently reduces the indemnification cap (no conspicuous call-out in summary pages; change appears only in the operative indemnity section).
- Converts the basket from a deductible basket to a tipping basket (once the threshold is exceeded, recoverable losses are measured from the first dollar).

C. Reconciliation to Schedules / Base Materials
Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. Because scheduled exceptions control over general plan statements, any reduction in cap or change in basket mechanics must be read together with the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability inventory. A lower cap plus a tipping basket re-prices the same retained-liability stack: the tipping feature increases expected recovery once the threshold is crossed, while the silent cap cut truncates upside and may leave Schedule 5.2 liabilities partially unbacked relative to the Debtor Plan's risk allocation and the valuation summary's residual-value assumptions.

The silent character of the cap reduction is itself a process deviation: confirmation and disclosure integrity require that economic shifts of this type be transparent in the disclosure statement excerpts and any valuation bridge provided to creditors and the court.

D. Risk Assessment
- Cap reduction: Adverse to the protected indemnified constituencies under the Debtor Plan; may impair feasibility optics if residual claims exceed the reduced cap; inconsistent with valuation summary support for the original indemnity backstop.
- Tipping basket: Increases expected indemnity outflow versus a pure deductible once losses clear the threshold; commercially meaningful but within the range the client has authorized to concede.
- Interaction with Schedule 5.2: Highest residual risk sits where retained liabilities approach or exceed the reduced cap.

E. Recommended Disposition
- Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): ACCEPT, per controlling deal-team instruction that the client will concede the basket conversion.
- Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT the silent reduction; COUNTER by restoring the Debtor Plan cap (or an expressly negotiated alternative cap) and requiring conspicuous disclosure of any agreed change in the disclosure statement and plan supplement. Do not permit a silent cap cut to ride on acceptance of the basket point.
- Require a Schedule 5.2 bring-down confirming that retained liabilities remain within the restored (or expressly re-cut) cap.

DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT DEFINITION; REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
Status: MATERIAL — Reject / Counter (do not accept carve-outs that neutralize known Schedule 3.7 risk)

A. Debtor Plan Baseline
The Debtor Plan MAE definition follows a conventional structure: MAE is measured against the reorganized enterprise / transaction basis without open-ended carve-outs that eliminate regulatory developments of the precise type already disclosed and live in the case.

B. Committee Markup
Adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter, narrowing the circumstances in which an MAE can be asserted by reference to regulatory developments.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules / Base Materials
Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. Under the governing rule that scheduled exceptions control over general statements, Schedule 3.7 establishes that regulatory-inquiry risk is known, live, and material to the disclosure package. Carving that same category of regulatory action out of MAE would:
- Nullify MAE protection precisely where Schedule 3.7 has flagged residual risk;
- Create a disclosure / plan inconsistency: the disclosure statement excerpts and schedules put creditors on notice of the inquiries, while the MAE definition would simultaneously treat related regulatory action as non-MAE;
- Shift downside from the party that sought MAE protection under the Debtor Plan to the reorganized estate / other constituencies without a corresponding economic concession.

D. Risk Assessment
High. Accepting the carve-outs would allow the Committee Markup to use Schedule 3.7 knowledge as a sword (to exclude the risk from MAE) rather than a shield (to qualify representations). In a restructuring context, that undermines conditionality, termination, and related plan-support constructs that reference MAE, and weakens the narrative consistency of the disclosure statement.

E. Recommended Disposition
- REJECT the new regulatory-action MAE carve-outs as proposed.
- COUNTER: (i) retain Debtor Plan MAE coverage for regulatory action; (ii) if any limited carve-out is eventually negotiated, confine it to ordinary-course regulatory administration expressly excluding the two pending inquiries on Schedule 3.7 and any expansion, adverse finding, fine, consent decree, or operational restriction arising from them; (iii) add an express schedule-priority clause confirming that Schedule 3.7 disclosures do not themselves constitute or expand MAE carve-outs; (iv) align disclosure-statement MAE risk-factor language with the final MAE definition so the plan, schedules, and disclosure statement speak with one voice.

DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
Status: MATERIAL — WALK-AWAY (reject any survival-period reduction)

A. Debtor Plan Baseline
Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for representations and related claim periods. That matrix is the controlling temporal architecture for core representations under the base materials. General plan text is subordinate to Exhibit B where they conflict.

B. Committee Markup
Introduces a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules / Base Materials
Exhibit B is the operative survival schedule. The markup's shortened limitation period directly contradicts Exhibit B. Because scheduled exceptions / exhibit mechanics control over general statements, the Exhibit B matrix prevails unless and until Exhibit B is expressly amended through a negotiated plan supplement or modified exhibit — not through a silent or lightly marked limitation-period insert in the plan body.

Shortened survival also interacts with Deviations 1 and 2: a lower indemnity cap (Deviation 1) and weakened MAE construct (Deviation 2) already compress substantive protection; truncating the time to assert core-representation claims compounds that compression and may leave Schedule 5.2 retained-liability and Schedule 3.7 regulatory issues time-barred before they mature into quantifiable losses.

D. Risk Assessment
Critical / walk-away. Per the controlling partner instruction, the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier thread messages with the opposite priority ordering are superseded.

E. Recommended Disposition
- REJECT in full any reduction to the survival / limitation period applicable to core representations.
- REQUIRE express conformity to Exhibit B; any future change must be effected by a marked revision to Exhibit B itself, with client sign-off.
- Designate this issue WALK-AWAY: do not package survival concessions with acceptance of the basket conversion or other committee asks.
- Confirm in the plan supplement and disclosure-statement excerpts that claim-assertion periods track Exhibit B without abbreviation.

IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION (MARKUP × SCHEDULES × VALUATION / DISCLOSURE)

1. Valuation summary consistency. The Debtor Plan's indemnity cap and survival matrix support the residual-risk and recoveries implied by the valuation summary. A silent cap cut (Deviation 1) and shortened survival (Deviation 3) undercut that support and should be reversed or expressly re-underwritten in any updated valuation bridge before solicitation.

2. Disclosure-statement excerpts. Transparency failures (silent cap reduction; MAE carve-outs that collide with Schedule 3.7; survival text that contradicts Exhibit B) create avoidable disclosure and confirmation risk. Each accepted or countered change must be reflected consistently in the disclosure statement and plan supplement.

3. Schedule priority rule (controlling interpretive canon).  
   - Schedule 3.7 controls MAE / regulatory risk framing → blocks Committee MAE carve-outs as drafted.  
   - Schedule 5.2 controls retained-liability allocation → requires restoring or expressly re-cutting the indemnity cap in light of listed liabilities; basket conversion may be accepted without disturbing this point.  
   - Exhibit B controls survival → blocks shortened limitation period; walk-away if pressed.

4. Transmittal / process. The committee's silent cap reduction should be called out in any response transmittal as a non-accepted economic shift, separate from the conceded basket point, to preserve a clear negotiation record.

V. DISPOSITION MATRIX (CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION APPLIED)

| # | Topic | Debtor Plan / Exhibit Baseline | Committee Markup | Schedule / Exhibit Control | Client Priority | Disposition |
|---|--------|--------------------------------|------------------|----------------------------|-----------------|-------------|
| 1a | Indemnification basket | Deductible basket | Tipping basket | Schedule 5.2 (liability inventory; economics shift) | Client will concede basket conversion | ACCEPT tipping basket |
| 1b | Indemnification cap | Baseline cap | Silent reduction | Schedule 5.2 | Protect economics / disclosure integrity | REJECT silent reduction; COUNTER to restore baseline (or expressly negotiate and disclose any new cap) |
| 2 | MAE – regulatory carve-outs | No carve-out for at-issue regulatory action | Carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue | Schedule 3.7 (two pending inquiries) | Preserve MAE for known regulatory risk | REJECT as drafted; COUNTER with Schedule 3.7–protective language |
| 3 | Survival / limitation period for core reps | Exhibit B survival matrix | Shortened limitation period | Exhibit B controls | Walk-away if reduced | REJECT; WALK-AWAY; require Exhibit B conformity |

VI. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS

1. Transmit a marked response plan / issues list implementing the Disposition Matrix: accept basket conversion only; restore indemnity cap; delete regulatory MAE carve-outs (or cabin them off Schedule 3.7 matters); restore Exhibit B survival periods.
2. Circulate an updated Schedule 5.2 / cap adequacy check and a Schedule 3.7 MAE alignment note to the deal team before the next committee session.
3. Revise disclosure-statement excerpts and any valuation bridge so they match the post-negotiation indemnity, MAE, and survival package — no silent economics.
4. Escalate immediately if the committee re-asserts survival-period reduction; per controlling instruction, that issue ends the current concession path.
5. Do not incorporate or rely on misfiled unrelated correspondence in any subsequent draft or filing.

VII. CONCLUSION

The Committee Markup is largely confirmatory of the Debtor Plan architecture but embeds three targeted economic and protective shifts. Reconciled against Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B, and applied under the controlling client instruction:

- Accept the deductible-to-tipping basket conversion.
- Reject the silent indemnification-cap reduction and counter to restore the baseline cap with full disclosure.
- Reject the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted and counter to protect Schedule 3.7 risk.
- Reject any shortening of core-representation survival; treat survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue and insist on Exhibit B conformity.

This disposition addresses every identified deviation in the counterparty markup, gives controlling effect to the schedules and exhibits over general plan text, and implements only the latest deal-team priority instruction.

— End of Report —
